Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Development actions

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

RSY_DEV=1 enables development command submission in the Godot adapter. The authority admits Dev_Spawn only from its local player seat. The shared model defaults to rejecting it, including when used without the Godot adapter. A remote client cannot grant itself permission by enabling its own flag or constructing an action packet. Dedicated servers without a local player seat do not admit it.

dev_spawn(kind, relative_seat, dx, dy) returns an action sequence when submitted. The final verdict arrives through normal action results; submission is not proof of acceptance. Spawn is an ordinary replayable reducer operation, using the entity pool and updating query history. Relative positions clamp to the original 40-pixel arena margin. Capacity or invalid-state refusal cannot partially spawn an entity. Accepted decisions use the existing action log, deduplication and checkpoints.

The pure game.action procedure intentionally performs no external permission lookup. Run transport-facing requests through the model's admission hook. A custom adapter that replaces that hook must preserve the development-command restriction as well as its own checks. The Godot adapter combines it with spray admission.

dev_walk(x, y, enabled) is a test input driver. It navigates around authored cover and stops within 35 pixels of the target; it does not teleport or edit saved state. It is useful for reproducible setup before an interaction.

The gauntlet test uses this path after all three waves/rests. Players stop fighting and walk to a clear setup area; only the host then spawns the original two barrels at offsets (150, 0) and (150, 50). The guest's attempted development spawn must receive an Invalid verdict. One ordinary host shot must cause both barrel blasts, without another clear reward, before all peers compare the complete world.

Adding the development action changed the schema fingerprint and introduced Scrapyard content ID 0x5253435241503041. Archives and peers from before that transition require explicit conversion/update. They are rejected rather than interpreted under the changed schema. Profile values were unchanged by that transition. The save guide records the current content identity and accepted conversion inputs.
